{"lens":"SAFETY_BYPASS","slice":"024B-core","reviewer":"sonnet-r1-safety_bypass","round":1,"verdict":"APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS","summary":"The 024B-core slice ships three safety-relevant components. Verified correct under the SAFETY_BYPASS lens: the fail-closed default for absent/unrecognised cascade-status routes empty command-substitution output through the `*)` die branch — Python failure yields empty `cascade_status`, which does not match `\"not applicable\"`, so FAIL-CLOSED is preserved. The exactly-one-match assertion on cascade-status (Python `re.findall`, exits 1 on ≠1 match) and on log-entry target (`parse_entry_repo`, exits 1 on ≠1 match) correctly resist multi-occurrence and phantom-target injection respectively. Path normalization via `readlink -f`/`os.path.realpath` precedes denylist evaluation; macOS `/var/log` → `/private/var/log` canonicalization is Darwin-gated and tested. Bootstrap-only guard (exit 1) fires at line 48-50, before the SHA non-existence check (exit 2, line 148-151). Wrapper template permissions are `contents: read` + `statuses: write` only — no `id-token: write` or `attestations: write` — and the fork-PR `if:` clause is present and tested. Adopter-slug canonicalization correctly converts `.` and `_` to `-`; `re.escape(slug)` defends against regex injection; case 4h verifies `jrnb2024/repo.foo_bar` → `jrnb2024-repo-foo-bar`. Worked-example matrix ex1+ex2 pass; ex3-ex6 verified to fail in test cases 4c-4f. Two MAJ findings identified: (1) `cascade-status: not applicable` exits 0 with zero enforcement — no technical constraint prevents cohort cascade slices 024C-F from declaring it; (2) `branch_log_modified` detection uses exact-path grep against `gh pr diff --name-only` output, which is unspecified for renamed files, creating a `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` negative-assertion bypass via log-file rename. Two MIN and two nit findings complete the set. No CRIT found.","findings":[{"id":"SAFE-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"`cascade-status: not applicable` exits 0 with NO enforcement checks. The script imposes no technical constraint preventing a cohort cascade slice (024C-F) from declaring this value. All log-entry, target-match, and TF-reference checks are bypassed; CI exits 0 with a success-class message, leaving the invocation-log audit trail unverified.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:140-143 — `\"not applicable\"` branch prints `OK: ... not a cohort cascade slice — nothing to enforce` and exits 0 before `target_repo` extraction, `branch_log_modified` check, or TF-reference validation fire. Test case 15b confirms exit 0 even when STATUS.md and DISPATCH-NOTE contain other cascade-status artefacts. No test, schema, or runtime check prevents 024C-F DISPATCH-NOTEs from using this value.","impact":"A 024C-F DISPATCH-NOTE declaring `cascade-status: not applicable` (e.g. copied from 024B-core template without updating) passes CI exit 0. The invocation-log entry is never required, the target repo is never verified, and the TF-reference check never fires. The primary audit trail for `enable-required-check.sh` invocations can be silently omitted; the only guard is single-operator self-review (D-031).","mitigation":"Require a second discriminating declaration before accepting `not applicable`: e.g. require DISPATCH-NOTE to also contain a `slice-type: tooling` header line, or maintain an allowlist of tooling-slice IDs against which `not applicable` is permitted. This adds a second declaration that code review can verify and that cannot be accidentally copied."},{"id":"SAFE-MAJ-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"In `--pr` mode, `branch_log_modified` is set via `grep -Fxq \"$BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG_REPO_REL\" <<<\"$changed_files\"` (exact original-path match). A PR that renames the branch-protection-log file may produce `gh pr diff --name-only` output that includes only the new path, leaving `branch_log_modified=0` despite log content being moved or added under the new path.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:174-177 — detection is a single exact-path grep with no rename-detection guard. `gh pr diff --name-only` rename behaviour is unspecified; GitHub rename detection may emit only the new path. `--diff-base` mode (`git diff --name-only`) similarly has no explicit `--no-renames` guard. No test case covers the rename scenario.","impact":"A `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` PR that renames `branch-protection-log.md` (moving new log content to the renamed file) passes the `branch_log_modified==0` negative assertion. An undisclosed `enable-required-check.sh` invocation record exists under the new path while CI asserts no log modification occurred, defeating the core R3-safety property (bypass via concurrent invocation + conflict-declaration). CODEOWNERS protection constrains but does not technically prevent the attack.","mitigation":"Enumerate both old and new paths for renames: use `git diff --diff-filter=ACDMRT --name-only` (listing both paths) or explicitly check for any path matching `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/*.md` in the changed-files list. Alternatively, compare the log file's content hash at DIFF_BASE and HEAD rather than relying solely on path-presence detection."},{"id":"SAFE-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"`canonicalize_adopter_slug` collapses `.`, `_`, and `-` to `-`, producing identical slugs for distinct adopter repos (e.g. `owner/repo.foo`, `owner/repo_foo`, `owner/repo-foo` all yield `owner-repo-foo`). A PR for a new adopter whose canonical slug collides with a previously-onboarded adopter would accept the existing TF row, bypassing the `onboarded-operator-bump` or `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` checks.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:93-99 — `re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9-]+\", \"-\", s.replace(\"/\", \"-\"))` merges all non-alphanumeric/hyphen chars to `-`. Plan-doc §2 states \"Plan-doc spec ensures unique-per-cohort\" as a documentation constraint only. Current 5-cohort (pim, recommender, shopify-app, mapp-doc-agent, control-tower) produces no collisions; exploitable only with future adopters.","impact":"For the current 5-cohort, no collision is possible. For future estate expansion, a prior onboarded adopter's `TF-024X-renovate-owner-repo-foo` row satisfies the `onboarded-operator-bump` STATUS.md check for a new adopter `owner/repo.foo` that produces the same canonical slug, allowing the new adopter to close without a distinct TF row. The cross-adopter false-positive passes CI silently.","mitigation":"Document the slug-collision surface explicitly in D-044's trust-model claims. Optionally add a uniqueness assertion at adoption time: reject any new adopter whose canonical slug already appears in existing TF rows in branch-protection-log or STATUS.md."},{"id":"SAFE-MIN-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"`--dispatch-note` and `--status-md` paths are normalized with `os.path.normpath` (resolves `.`/`..` but NOT symlinks), while `--branch-protection-log` receives full `os.path.realpath` resolution plus an explicit repo-root containment check. A symlink passed as `--dispatch-note` is silently followed to an out-of-repo target.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:89-103 — `normalize_path()` uses `os.path.normpath`; `BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG_REAL` uses `os.path.realpath` with `case \"$BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG_REAL\" in \"$REPO_ROOT\"|\"$REPO_ROOT\"/*) ;;`. No equivalent containment check for `DISPATCH_NOTE` or `STATUS_MD`. The asymmetry is structural, not incidental.","impact":"An operator passing `--status-md /symlink/to/external/file` where the external file contains a line matching the TF-024X regex would produce a false-positive pass for `onboarded-operator-bump`. The cascade-status regex is unlikely to match arbitrary files (fail-closed in practice), but the inconsistent treatment is a hardening gap and a trust-model inaccuracy in D-044's claim that path inputs are repo-contained.","mitigation":"Apply `os.path.realpath` + repo-root containment check to `--dispatch-note` and `--status-md` consistently with `--branch-protection-log`. The existing `REPO_ROOT` realpath computation (line 105-109) can be reused."},{"id":"SAFE-nit-001","severity":"nit","claim":"`parse_entry_repo` branch segment character class `[A-Za-z0-9._./-]` contains redundant duplicate characters: `.` and `_` each appear twice.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:185 — `r\"^###\\s+.+\\s+—\\s+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+(?:/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?)@([A-Za-z0-9._./-]+)$\"` — the branch capture group `[A-Za-z0-9._./-]` has two `.` and two `_`.","impact":"No security impact; the character class matches correctly. Purely cosmetic.","mitigation":"Replace `[A-Za-z0-9._./-]` with `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`."},{"id":"SAFE-nit-002","severity":"nit","claim":"Test harness covers two DIFFERENT cascade-status values (case 15) and one indented+unindented same-value pair (case 14), but does not explicitly test two identical unindented cascade-status values in a single DISPATCH-NOTE.","evidence":"tests/check_invocation_log/test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh:437-473 — cases 14 and 15 cover adjacent terrain. Code analysis confirms FAIL-CLOSED behavior (Python `re.findall` returns 2 matches → exits 1 → `cascade_status=\"\"` → `*)` die), but no test explicitly exercises this exact path.","impact":"No vulnerability; code is fail-closed in this scenario. Test coverage gap only.","mitigation":"Add a case with two identical unindented `cascade-status: onboarded` lines; assert non-zero exit with stderr containing `expected exactly one cascade-status match, found 2`."}]}
